run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The astronomy-shop stack was (re)deployed as a whole at 21:56:28Z, about 90 s before the end of the authorized window, so almost no pre-change telemetry exists (Prometheus' first sample is 21:56:54Z, Jaeger's first spans 21:57:26Z). All 27 application pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts, all 17 blackbox targets are up, Kafka has no under-replicated or offline partitions, and payment logged a successful 'Transaction complete' at 21:57:32Z. The one non-Helm mutation in the window is on the edge entry point: Deployment frontend-proxy/astronomy-shop went to generation 2 / revision 2 via managedFields manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 21:57:38Z, replacing its stock Envoy process (/bin/sh -c 'envsubst < envoy.tmpl.yaml ... && exec envoy -c envoy.yaml') with a single-threaded Perl 'edge request filter' (/usr/bin/perl -e '<embedded script>') whose pod template sets WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true" and WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$". That script takes a user-controlled ?waf= query value and matches it against the regex in-process, then short-circuits any non-empty candidate with a local 200 "ok" instead of proxying. The regex has a nested quantifier and is a classic catastrophic-backtracking (ReDoS) pattern, and the proxy handles one connection at a time with blocking reads under a 100m CPU limit, so a crafted ?waf= value can stall the entire site edge; requests carrying any waf value also stop reaching frontend. I did NOT observe that trigger fire: only ~16 s of post-change traffic exists, the new pod emitted no readable log lines and no spans in the window, and normal requests still succeeded (frontend-proxy probe_success=1, 2.5 ms at 21:57:54Z; Envoy-era spans all 200). I therefore report the frontend-proxy deployment change as the fault-bearing object and root cause, with its impact as a supported mechanism but unverified realization, and conclusion partial. Rejected as causes: startup-ordering connection-refused noise (resolved before 21:57:32Z), flagd feature-flag fault injection (all 15 flags defaultVariant 'off'), and Kafka/blackbox dependency faults.

claims.text: All 27 pods in namespace astronomy-shop are Running and ready with 0 container restarts; every pod started between 21:56:28Z and 21:57:38Z, i.e. the whole application was freshly deployed inside the window (individual pods include accounting-5897477844-jpbpv, frontend-6859c775df-6lbcr, frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-l86sg, payment-556cf8d457-wbphs).

Deployment frontend-proxy in namespace astronomy-shop is at generation 2 / deployment revision 2; its managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 21:56:28Z, then an Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 21:57:38Z, then kube-controller-manager status at 21:57:39Z. No other astronomy-shop deployment shows a non-helm manager or generation > 1.

The current frontend-proxy pod template runs command [/usr/bin/perl, -e] with a single embedded argument implementing an 'edge request filter', and sets env WAF_RULE_REGEX="^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" and WAF_RULE_ENABLED="true"; container resources are limits cpu=100m, memory=65Mi and the only port is 8080.

The same frontend-proxy pod template carries annotations edge.platform/change-ticket="EDGE-1847" and edge.platform/filter-profile="managed-rules-v2", and the embedded Perl script reads the candidate from a '?waf=' query parameter, evaluates the candidate against WAF_RULE_REGEX when WAF_RULE_ENABLED is not "false", prints a request_filter_eval record with elapsedSeconds, and for any non-empty candidate answers HTTP 200 "ok" locally instead of forwarding to frontend.

Two frontend-proxy ReplicaSets exist: frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (created 21:56:29Z, now replicas 0) whose container command was /bin/sh -c 'envsubst < envoy.tmpl.yaml | sed ... > envoy.yaml && exec envoy -c envoy.yaml', and frontend-proxy-88764bfbb (created 21:57:38Z, 1 ready replica) whose command is /usr/bin/perl -e with the WAF filter script and WAF_RULE_REGEX/WAF_RULE_ENABLED env; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-frontend-proxy.

The superseded frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5-xrfds was running Envoy (log lines about envoy filters, 'caught ENVOY_SIGTERM', 'shutting down server instance', 'exiting' at 21:57:39Z) and a Killing event 'Stopping container frontend-proxy' for that pod is timestamped 21:57:39Z, matching the rollout caused by the 21:57:38Z deployment update.

Before the rollout, frontend-proxy (Envoy) spans at 21:57:32-21:57:34Z show GET and 'router frontend egress' with http.status_code=200 and durations 5.1-24.9 ms, i.e. normal edge latency on the stock proxy.

At 21:57:54Z the blackbox probe of frontend-proxy.astronomy-shop:8080 still reported probe_success=1 with probe_duration_seconds=0.0025, and all 17 astronomy-shop blackbox targets (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation, shipping) reported up=1.

Between 21:57:20Z and 21:57:54Z the only error-like lines from non-collector astronomy-shop apps were kafka JMX 'Created Counter for kafka.request.failed' info lines, two python OTel exporter warnings from recommendation/product-reviews, one accounting stderr line 'libgssapi_krb5.so.2: cannot open shared object file', and a product-reviews INFO line stating 'llmRateLimitError feature flag: False'.

The flagd-config ConfigMap holds 15 ENABLED flags (llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak) and every one of them has defaultVariant "off".
The Kafka cluster reports 1 broker, 2 topics, 51 partitions, 0 under-replicated partitions, 0 offline partitions and no offline brokers at query time.

The load-generator fail ratio went from 0.5625 at 21:57:24Z to 0 at 21:57:54Z while running 2 locust processes with 10 users, and the locust-fetcher error payload at 21:57:35Z lists only ConnectionRefusedError/503 errors from the just-restarted stack.

Frontend and payment logged connect ECONNREFUSED to in-cluster ClusterIPs during bring-up: frontend to 10.96.244.97:8080 (cart) and 10.96.212.144:8080 (checkout) at 21:56:56-21:57:04Z, and payment to 10.96.62.58:8013 (flagd) at 21:57:19Z; payment subsequently logged 'Transaction complete.' with transactionId 8c69b4bb-8657-433b-bc0b-9a5aedb83bb5 at 21:57:32Z.

The 21:57:38Z mutation of Deployment frontend-proxy is the injected fault: the edge entry point now evaluates the user-controlled ?waf= value against the catastrophic-backtracking regex "^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" inside a single-threaded, blocking Perl accept loop with a 100m CPU limit, so one crafted request can peg the process and stall the whole site edge (customer-visible hangs/timeouts), while any request carrying a non-empty waf value is answered locally with 200 "ok" and never reaches frontend. The rule's own elapsedSeconds field is the instrument that would record such a stall.

Alternative not yet excluded: the 21:57:38Z frontend-proxy change could be an authorised edge-filter rollout ('EDGE-1847', profile 'managed-rules-v2') and the real fault could lie outside what the sampled window shows; no other object in the window shows a non-Helm mutation, a crash, an eviction/OOM or application error lines attributable to it, so this alternative has no supporting evidence yet.

Startup-ordering connection refusals are not the root cause: they occur at 21:56:56-21:57:19Z while the namespace was still coming up after the 21:56:28Z helm deploy, and stop once peers listen (payment transaction completes at 21:57:32Z, all blackbox targets up at 21:57:54Z).

flagd feature-flag fault injection is not the cause: all 15 ENABLED fault flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap have defaultVariant "off", and product-reviews logged 'llmRateLimitError feature flag: False' at 21:57:24Z.

Normal-path edge traffic was still healthy seconds after the frontend-proxy rollout: the blackbox probe of frontend-proxy returned success in 2.5 ms at 21:57:54Z, and the sampled spans for frontend-proxy before the replacement were all http.status_code=200 with 5-25 ms durations, so no observed customer-facing failure can yet be attributed to the new filter.

Treat Deployment frontend-proxy/astronomy-shop revision 2 as suspect: diff it against ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 (Envoy command, no WAF env), and either revert the pod template to the Envoy entrypoint or, if the edge filter must stay, replace the nested-quantifier rule "^([a-zA-Z]+)*$" with a linear-time validation, feed the candidate from a bounded field, and stop answering 200 locally for matched requests; then confirm by sending a long non-matching ?waf= value and watching request_filter_eval elapsedSeconds and edge latency.

gaps: No baseline before the incident: Prometheus' earliest sample in this target is 21:56:54Z and Jaeger's earliest spans in returned queries are 21:57:26Z, while the whole stack was deployed at 21:56:28Z, so no comparable pre-change latency/error baseline exists (no latency trend is claimed).

Only ~16 s of traffic after the 21:57:38Z frontend-proxy rollout (window ends 21:57:54Z), so the ReDoS/short-circuit behaviour of the new filter was not observed happening; no request with a ?waf= parameter was found in the evidence.

The new frontend-proxy pod emitted no readable output: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-proxy-88764bfbb-l86sg returned zero lines (pod has no previous container instance), and no cAdvisor series for its perl container appeared up to 21:57:54Z (only the registry.k8s.io/pause container), so request_filter_eval records and CPU saturation of the new proxy are unobservable in this Run.

Queries for error-tagged frontend and checkout traces in 21:57:39-21:57:54Z returned no_data (not citable), and traces_search_by_tags/grafana queries restricted to pod=~"frontend-proxy-88764bfbb.*" also returned nothing; the trace-error status of the window therefore remains unchecked rather than clean.

Identity and intent of the managedFields manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' that updated Deployment frontend-proxy at 21:57:38Z are unknown; the change_history integration is not configured, so no change record or audit trail can confirm who applied it or what the previous template value was.
ALERTS{alertstate="firing"} at 21:57:54Z returned no data (not citable), so the alert state at the incident boundary is unknown rather than 'no alerts'.
The Redis/Valkey dependency could not be checked (redis_info returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so valkey-cart health is unknown and not claimed healthy.

No metric series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_* or per-service ERROR counters were returned by this target (no_data), so per-service span error rates and request latencies could not be quantified; span evidence is a biased sample only.

Kubernetes object state and events were read at query time (21:57:57Z-22:00:15Z) and events cover only 20:57:32Z-21:57:39Z, so anything that happened earlier in the authorized 24 h window was not read.
next_steps: Diff Deployment frontend-proxy revision 2 against ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5 and revert the pod template to the Envoy entrypoint (or replace the nested-quantifier WAF regex) if the edge filter was not an intended change.

If the filter must stay, exercise it with a long non-matching ?waf= value in a canary and watch the request_filter_eval elapsedSeconds field plus frontend-proxy CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total) to confirm or refute the backtracking stall.

Collect change history / audit records for the 'OpenAPI-Generator' update at 21:57:38Z (change_history integration is not configured here) to establish who applied the frontend-proxy template change and under which ticket.
Re-check Redis/Valkey (valkey-cart), Prometheus alert state and per-service error spans from reachable sources to close the unchecked dependencies.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
